definition: Altercation means a noisy, heated dispute.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word altercation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know altercation should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: An altercation over the bill flared at the next table, and the whole cafe went quiet to listen.
A disagreement can stay perfectly civil — two views that simply differ; an altercation has already turned loud and heated.
A brawl goes past altercation: fists out, furniture over, a fight that needs more than a stern word to stop.

A quarrel is an angry back-and-forth that can run at any volume and any length — it can simmer quietly through a week of clipped exchanges. An altercation is louder and briefer: a dispute that flares up hot, in the moment, and is finished when the shouting stops. A quarrel can smolder; an altercation is the flare itself.

A squabble is a petty flare-up over something small — the last cookie, whose turn it is to drive — and the word itself belittles the fight. An altercation is a full-sized, noisy, heated dispute, serious enough to stop conversation nearby and pull a bystander in to end it.
an agreed pause in fighting
the mending that puts a fight to rest

Somewhere over Nebraska, two passengers discovered one overhead bin and two roller bags.
Voices rose; an elbow was thrown wide; a flight attendant arrived with the practiced calm of someone who has separated grown adults before.
By the time the seatbelt light chimed, both bags were stowed, both men were seated rows apart, and the whole altercation had lasted four minutes.
Altercation is the exact word for that four minutes: a dispute, a fight — loud, abrupt, and over.
It names the flare-up itself, not what led there and not what lingers after.
A grievance can smolder for years; an altercation is the moment it sparks, and when the shouting stops, the altercation is finished.
Altercation is the reporter's word for a dispute that flared — loud, brief, and usually over by the time anyone writes it down.
It names one incident; for the standing bad feeling between people, this unit offers hostility, and for hatred that has settled in for years, enmity.
If it came to blows and rolled on the floor, brawl says so.
